findings.location: row weirdml::2 fields version, version_status, status
findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 identifies the current board as 'WeirdML v3' and lists 'Previous versions: WeirdML v2 · WeirdML v1'. The row claims version '2', status 'active', version_status 'published'. The current protocol version is v3, so a v2 board cannot be presented as the active current identity; this is a release-version change reusing an existing identity.
findings.repair: Either align the row to the current WeirdML v3 identity (version 3) or demote this row to 'retained' and identify it as the historical v2 board; do not claim active v2 against a v3 page.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 states the official score is '80% normalized area under its line on a logarithmic token axis, plus 20% of its final value', over 11 tasks / 15 configurations, with 'Effective scores include normalization and hint penalties; they are not raw accuracy.' The row instead asserts 'Average Max Accuracy ... maximum test accuracy across the 5 iterations ... 17 tasks' and a PyTorch-code description. This directly contradicts the current protocol's metric and task count. The generated scale (162 values, low 1.729, high 93.573) fits unit 'percent'/range [0,100], but that only establishes scale, not metric meaning.
findings.repair: Replace the metric and description with the current v3 scoring rule (area-under-curve effective score, 11 tasks, 15 configurations, normalization/hint penalties) or explicitly source the v2 metric and change status to 'retained'.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 names WeirdML v3 as current and v2 as a previous version, showing v2 replaced going forward. The row sets status 'active' and superseded_by null, contradicting the page. The generated activity summary (2 changed avg_acc values) can support 'active' only for the board actually served today, which is v3, not v2.
findings.repair: Set status to 'retained' and set superseded_by to the registry id of the successor WeirdML v3 board, or change version/status to the current v3 board; do not keep v2 as active with no successor when the protocol names v3.

uncertainties: Hashes, transport and qualification checks cannot be executed in this review; supplied SHA bindings are relied on as given.

The exact registry id for successor WeirdML v3 is not in the packet, so the precise superseded_by value cannot be stated; null is nevertheless contradicted by SOURCE 1 naming v3 as current and v2 as a previous version.
The generated scale and activity summaries are the run's own reads and were used only as permitted by the criteria (scale for unit/range, activity for status evidence).
